claims.text: In uncharacterized high-entropy alloys, Tc is governed by local variations in electron–phonon coupling arising from controlled compositional fluctuations.
Changing the relative concentrations of strong- and weak-coupling elements tunes the density of states at the Fermi level.
Changes in the density of states at the Fermi level modulate Tc.
A high-entropy alloy contains at least five elements, each at no less than 5 at.%.
The proposed starting material is a fully mixed, single-phase, disordered solid solution.
The proposed starting material has a BCC lattice.
The baseline is drawn from a well-characterized Nb–Ta-rich superconducting HEA family.
Nb or Ta can be treated as a key strong electron–phonon-coupling element and replaced by a chemically similar element with a weaker coupling contribution.
The disordered BCC lattice manifests local compositional fluctuations.
Local compositional fluctuations modulate the local density of states at the Fermi level.
Substitution changes local electron–phonon coupling by modifying the density of states at the Fermi level.
A larger contribution from strong-coupling elements enhances pairing and raises Tc, whereas reducing those elements lowers Tc.
Increasing the strong-coupling element fraction should increase Tc, while reducing it should decrease Tc relative to the baseline.
The compositional trend in Tc should be accompanied by shifts in phonon modes or superconducting gap magnitude.
The benchmark Nb–Ta-rich HEA has Tc around 7–8 K.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the alloys remain single-phase, disordered BCC solid solutions without phase separation or ordering.
Lattice distortion may independently influence superconducting properties.
Failure of systematic composition changes to produce corresponding Tc and electron–phonon-coupling shifts would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is framed as explaining an uncharacterized HEA, but the specified starting material and benchmark are assigned to the well-characterized Nb–Ta-rich family. This makes it unclear whether the proposed test addresses an uncharacterized system outside the established class or merely modifies a member of that class.
